excerpt: Primer began in 2020 as online homeschooling tools and kids' clubs, then pivoted to in-person microschools. It now runs teacher-led K–8 schools focused on reading, writing and math, with tuition often covered by state scholarships.
content:
Primer is an education company that runs small, teacher-led private schools, known as microschools, for children from kindergarten to eighth grade. Its website describes a fundamentals-focused model inspired by the primers of early American education, built on mastering reading, writing and maths, with safe, caring classrooms and combined-age classes. Fortune reported in 2025 on Liberty City Primer, a Primer microschool in Miami with six classrooms and a few dozen students, led by a former public school teacher who runs it as her own school with Primer's support.

Primer did not start this way. TechCrunch reported in May 2020 that founder Ryan Delk, who was himself homeschooled from kindergarten through eighth grade, was building full-stack infrastructure for parents to homeschool their children, and had raised a $3.7 million seed round led by Founders Fund. Its early online products, including homeschooling resources and clubs for children, were meant to supplement a child's education. Contrary Research reported that Primer later shifted to in-person microschools, which became its core offering by December 2022, and that Delk is CEO.

Primer publishes tuition by state. Its tuition page says most Primer families pay between $0 and $3,000 a year, because it accepts state education savings accounts and scholarships such as Texas Education Freedom Accounts, Florida's Step Up for Students scholarships and Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Accounts. In Texas, families earning $75,000 or less who receive Education Freedom Account funding pay nothing out of pocket; in Florida, out-of-pocket tuition ranges from $0 to $6,752 a year depending on household income.

This profile draws on Primer's own pages and published reporting. We have not visited a Primer school, and nothing here is paid placement.
